title: Thermal dynamics of metabotropic glutamate receptor signaling revealed by subtraction micro-calorimetric measurements on live cells
protocol: Cultivate wild-type CHO \(CHO-k1) cells and CHO-mGluR1α cells in 25 cm² cell culture flasks with 10 mL DMEM/F12 medium.
Grow cells to confluence in the presence of humidified air, 5% CO₂, at 37°C.
Pass cells once per week and allow them to grow to 70% confluence between passages.
Check receptor activity once per week by fura-2 based Ca²⁺ imaging using a fraction of the CHO-mGluR1α cells.
Stabilize the ITC system continuously run at room temperature set as close to the recording temperature level.
Maintain the ITC system by loading degassed ultra-pure water \(1.8 mL) in the recording chamber and setting the room temperature at 22 ± 0.5°C.
Routinely test system conditions once a week by repeated titration of ultra-pure water \(10 μL).
Degas the recording buffer (BSS containing 0.5 mM CaCl₂; 5 mL × 2 tubes) for 10 min at 18°C using a Thermo Vac degasser.
Warm up Versene and PBS using a water bath at 37°C for 10 min.
Aspirate DMEM/F12 medium from the culture flask.
Rinse cells with 3 mL of PBS twice in the clean bench.
Replace PBS with 5 mL of Versene.
Place the flask containing Versene in a CO₂ incubator for 5 min.
Gently wash cells with Versene using an electronic pipette to remove them from adhering to the flask and generate a cell suspension.
Pool cells from two flasks into one centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the pooled cells at 1000 rpm for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in degassed 0.5 mM CaCl₂ BSS (5 mL) in a Thermo Vac tube.
Suspend cells gently 10 times using a 1 mL PIPETMAN.
Load 20 μl of cell suspension into a hemocytometer and count the cell density on an inverted microscope.
Adjust the cell density to 6×10^5 cells/ml using degassed 0.5 mM CaCl2 BSS.
Transfer 3 mL of cell suspension supplemented with 3 μl of protease inhibitor cocktail to a Thermo Vac plastic tube.
Adjust the temperature to 18°C (2°C below recording temperature) for 5 min in the Thermo Vac.
Replace ultrapure water in the recording chamber with degassed 0.5 mM CaCl2 BSS at 18°C using a long needle Hamilton syringe, repeating twice for complete rinsing.
Load 2.5 mL of cell suspension into a long needle Hamilton syringe and gently fill the recording chamber with 2 mL total volume.
Suspend cells in the recording chamber by gentle pipetting (2-3 times).
Remove excessive volume (0.2 mL) of cell suspension together with any accidentally generated air bubbles using the long needle syringe.
Seal the recording chamber with a Teflon cap after visual confirmation that it is filled with suspension.
Set total injections to 11 times.
Set cell temperature to 20°C.
Set reference power to 10 μcal/s.
Set initial delay to 600 s.
Set stirring speed to 310 rpm.
Set feedback mode gain to high feedback.
Set injection volume to 10 µl (first injection volume to 2 µl).
Set duration of the first injection to 4 s.
Set duration of the second to eleventh injections to 20 s.
Set spacing among injections to 800 s.
Set filter period to 2 s.
Run pre-stirred equilibration and monitor DP values on the screen.
Confirm DP values are between 7.0-8.5 µcal/s until 30 min after running.
Terminate recordings if the DP value is smaller than 7 µcal/s to check for errors.
Rinse the tip of the titration needle by flushing with BSS using a 1 mL PIPETMAN.
Set the titration syringe and run the final baseline equilibration.
Monitor DP values until they reach 8.5 μcal/s or more.
Terminate recordings if DP values are less than 8.5 µcal/s or unstable after 3 hours.
Initiate titrations.
Repeat procedures using control CHO-k1 cells after rinsing recording chamber with ultrapure water.
Confirm cell viability using calcein-AM and propidium iodide at the end of recordings.
Subtract receptor-mediated thermal responses to yield heat absorption and production data.
Conduct repeated measurements using different cells at different times for increased accuracy.
